problem:
Find the general solution to the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-y=\sqrt{y}.
$$

feedback.problem:
The substitution $z={y}^{m}$ for some real number $m$ transforms the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+{x}^{2}y=\frac{{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{y}}
$$

into an equation of the form ${z}^{′}(x)+P(x)z(x)=Q(x).$ What is the function $P(x)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that our equation is an instance of the Bernoulli differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+p(x)y=q(x){y}^{n}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
p(x)={x}^{2},\,q(x)={x}^{3},\,n=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

First, we multiply the differential equation by ${y}^{1/2},$ and we get

$$
{y}^{1/2}\frac{dy}{dx}+{x}^{2}{y}^{3/2}={x}^{3}.\,\,(∗)
$$

Then, we make the substitution

$$
z={y}^{1-n}={y}^{3/2}.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get 

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,{y}^{1/2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{3}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}.
$$

 

Therefore, equation $(∗)$ can be written as a linear equation in $z(x)$ as follows:

$$
\frac{2}{3}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+{x}^{2}\,z={x}^{3}
$$

Finally, we write the above equation in standard form, which gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}\,z=\frac{3{x}^{3}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}.$
